approach: Add a code_health module in athena-core. Pure functions measure files: production lines (syn parses the file, drops #[cfg(test)] modules by span and counts the remaining lines), longest function (syn, fn/impl/trait items, line spans), 7-day churn, failure citations, and test run time. A threshold function turns the numbers into breaches. An orchestrator `Athena::code_health_after_landing(ui)` runs after a landing. It queues one structural-pass request per breached file through Athena::queue, deduplicated against open requests. It counts landings since a new typed baseline record (AnyRecord::CodeHealthBaseline, athena.code-health-baseline/1). The first landing writes the baseline and queues no review. Every 10th landing after it queues a self-contained high-priority design-review request and writes a new baseline. The check is called from Athena::land_pr after resync_onto_merge and the Pages watch, and from note_finished in steward.rs, before its early return for nested runs and non-landed outcomes is applied to the steward only. It never fails the landing and only logs a warning. The status view gets a code-health table that display.rs renders with aligned columns.

decisions.choice: Measure function length with syn (full, span-locations feature), counting production lines as the file's lines minus the line spans of #[cfg(test)] modules.
decisions.reason: Buy over build: syn gives exact function spans and cfg attributes, which a line scan gets wrong for nested braces, strings and macros. Recorded in docs/decisions.md.

rejected.why: Breaks on braces in strings, comments and macros, and tracks cfg(test) poorly.

rejected.option: Shell out to a lint tool
rejected.why: Adds an external dependency and is not reproducible in tests.

decisions.choice: A landing is a first-parent commit on HEAD. The 7-day churn, the 'landings per file per week' and the 10-landing cadence all come from git log on HEAD. The baseline stores the first-parent commit count it was set at; a review is due when the current count minus the baseline count is at least 10.
decisions.reason: It is idempotent: both hooks can run for the same landing and the counter does not double count. In land_pr no outcome record exists yet, so counting Outcome records would miss the landing. Writing a new baseline when a review is queued stops repeat reviews.

rejected.option: A counter file incremented per hook call
rejected.why: Double counts when both hooks fire, and is not reloadable from git.
Not yet written when land_pr's hook runs.

decisions.choice: Name the new record CodeHealthBaseline (schema athena.code-health-baseline/1, path records/code-health/<month>/<id>.json), separate from the existing per-job Baseline. Records gets a code_health_baselines Vec; the latest by created_at is current.
decisions.reason: AnyRecord::Baseline already exists for per-job check baselines; reusing it would conflict. It is a typed record in git, so Records::load restores it into a fresh state directory.

rejected.option: A file in the state directory
rejected.why: Lost on a fresh state directory; criterion 4 needs it to survive reload from git.

decisions.choice: Structural-pass request text starts with a fixed marker line 'Structural pass: <path>' and lists the measured numbers and acceptance bullets. Dedupe: skip a file when any non-closed job in Records has a request starting with that marker for the path.
decisions.reason: Gives exactly one request per breach, and a second run queues none while the first is open.

rejected.option: Dedupe by a record of past requests
rejected.why: Would block a new request after the old one closes and the file is still over.

decisions.choice: Design-review text is built in full by a function and passed to Athena::queue, then set_priority to high (or a 'Priority: high' line in the text, since plan reads that).
decisions.reason: No design-review role exists, so the request must carry its own content. A 'Priority: high' line is honored by plan and needs no second commit.

decisions.choice: Test run time is read from a small file the checks already write if one exists; otherwise it shows as 'unknown'. Citations are counted from jobs whose outcome is Rejected or Failed (and planning stops) with a candidate change entry for the file.
decisions.reason: Uses records already held; no new measurement runs inside status.

files.purpose: Measure, threshold, citations, queue structural passes and design reviews, baseline logic, and the tests.
Declare `pub mod code_health` and document it.
Add a code_health field to StatusView, filled by Athena::status.
Call the check in land_pr after resync_onto_merge and the Pages watch; add a hook test.
Render the code-health table with aligned headers in status().
Call the check in note_finished when a job lands (also in nested runs, which skip only the steward).
Only if needed: expose a helper the check uses to read outcomes; go() already calls note_finished.
Add code_health_baselines to Records and fill it in the loader.
Only if needed: share the queue helper so a request can carry a 'Priority: high' line.
Add the CodeHealthBaseline struct, the AnyRecord variant, its schema, path and validation, and a round-trip test.
Add syn with the full and visit features and proc-macro2 span-locations.
Integration tests that both landing paths run the check, with the disk minimum at 0.
Record thresholds, the syn call, the baseline record and the 10-landing cadence.

steps: Read the workspace Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for syn and proc-macro2 versions; add syn (full, visit) and the proc-macro2 span-locations feature to athena-core.

In athena-data/src/records.rs add CodeHealthBaseline {id, created_at, landings, reason}, the AnyRecord variant with schema athena.code-health-baseline/1, path records/code-health/<month>/<id>.json, validation, and a round-trip test.
In store.rs add Records.code_health_baselines and fill it in the loader's match.

Write code_health.rs: measure_file (syn), thresholds, churn from git log --first-parent --since=7.days --name-only, citations from Records, report struct and a table row type, structural-pass text and dedupe, design-review text, baseline and cadence logic, and the `Athena::code_health_after_landing` method that swallows errors into a Ui line.
Wire the hooks: land_pr after the Pages watch block, and note_finished at its top for a Landed outcome, ahead of the nested and steward early return.
Add the code_health field to StatusView and fill it in Athena::status (measurement of the working tree, plus the suite time if recorded); render it in display.rs with aligned columns.
Write the tests listed in demonstrations, including code_health_hooks.rs, with min_free_gb = 0.
Run fmt, clippy and test; fix any exhaustive-match fallout.

risks.risk: The hook in land_pr runs in tests with a fake runner and a scratch repo; a failure there could break existing gh tests.
risks.mitigation: The check logs a warning and returns on any error, never failing the landing; it skips when the repo has no parseable Rust sources.

risks.risk: Existing code is large (gh.rs is over 200 KB), so the real repository would breach on the first run and queue many requests.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended behavior; the dedupe keeps it to one per file. Tests use fixture trees.

risks.risk: Adding an AnyRecord variant breaks exhaustive matches elsewhere (path, schema, job_of, parse validation).
risks.mitigation: Fix every match the compiler reports; the plan lists records.rs and store.rs.

risks.risk: Nested-run tests hit the disk guard.
risks.mitigation: Tests set [disk] min_free_gb = 0 as fixed in 3947eb3.

risks.risk: Workspace Cargo.toml and dependency lint rules (such as cargo-deny or xtask policy) may reject a new crate.
risks.mitigation: Check the workspace manifest and xtask policy tests before adding; syn is already in the lock file through derive crates, which limits new code.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in code_health.rs builds a temp tree with a source file containing a #[cfg(test)] mod, a 40-line function and a short one, a git history with dated landings, and fixture Records with rejected/failed jobs citing the file. It asserts the production line count, the longest function, landings in 7 days, and the citations.
demonstrations.observes: The measured numbers equal the fixture's known values; the test module's lines are not counted.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without syn-based spans the cfg(test) lines would be counted and the longest function would be wrong.

demonstrations.method: Tests for the threshold function and the whole check: a 2001-line file, a 201-line function, a 1501-line file with 5 landings in a week, and a 1000-line file with 3 landings.
demonstrations.observes: Each of the three conditions is reported with its reason; the small file is not flagged; boundary values (2000, 200, 1500 with 4) are not flagged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the thresholds, no breach would appear, or the under-threshold file would be flagged.

demonstrations.method: Test with a scratch repository: run the check after a landing with one breaching file, then load Records and read the queued request; run it again; then close the job and keep an open one.
demonstrations.observes: Exactly one queued request names the file and the measured numbers; the second run queues none; an open structural-pass request also queues none.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dedupe a second run would queue a second request.

demonstrations.method: A schema round-trip test in athena-data/src/records.rs (serialize, parse via AnyRecord::parse, check path and schema). A core test writes the baseline on the first landing, then loads Records::load from git into a fresh StateDir.
demonstrations.observes: The record round-trips and the baseline survives a reload from git; the first landing queued no review.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the record variant, the baseline would not parse or reload and the first landing would fire a review.

demonstrations.method: Test sets the baseline, then adds 9 landing commits and checks, then a 10th, using Athena::queue in a scratch repository with the disk minimum set to 0.
demonstrations.observes: No design-review request after 9; one request after the 10th, with priority high in Records; none again right after.
demonstrations.fails_without: A cadence off by one would queue on the 9th or not on the 10th.

demonstrations.method: Test reads the queued review's text from Records and checks the named review subjects and the design-only deliverable.
demonstrations.observes: The text names the code-health table, files most changed and most broken since the last review, open structural-pass requests, recent rejections and planning stops, and asks for a short design note with proposed changes as a design-only job.
demonstrations.fails_without: A text missing any of these phrases fails the assertions.

demonstrations.method: New integration test crates/athena-cli/tests/code_health_hooks.rs plus a unit test in gh.rs: each lands a job through land_pr (fake runner) and through note_finished, with min_free_gb set to 0, and asserts a structural-pass request exists afterwards. A companion check shows the request is absent when the hook call is removed (the test calls the pre-hook path with the hook disabled via the same test seam, or asserts on ordering after resync_onto_merge and the Pages watch).
demonstrations.observes: Both landing paths queue the request for a breaching file; the land_pr hook runs after the resync and the Pages watch in the ui line order.
demonstrations.fails_without: With either hook removed, its test finds no queued request.

demonstrations.method: Render test in display.rs builds a StatusView with code-health rows and a test time, calls status(), and asserts header and row alignment.
demonstrations.observes: The output has a 'code health' table with columns file, lines, longest fn, week, cited, limits, over, and the test suite time; column starts line up across all rows.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the table in status output the assertions on the header fail.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked

demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased has an entry; docs/decisions.md has a new decision with the thresholds (2000, 200, 1500 with 5 per week), the syn buy-versus-build call, the baseline record, and the 10-landing cadence.

open_questions: Whether every first-parent commit on HEAD counts as a landing (human commits too); chosen because it is idempotent and needs no outcome record. A reviewer may prefer only commits with an Athena-Job trailer.
Where the test-suite run time is recorded today; the plan shows 'unknown' if no record has it. The producer must grep checks.rs for a timing field and use it.
Whether syn's span-locations (proc-macro2) work outside a proc macro: they need the proc-macro2 'span-locations' feature, which must be added to the workspace dependencies.
Whether the workspace Cargo.toml pins dependencies centrally (the crate uses `.workspace = true`); then syn must be added there too, which is a governance-adjacent file not listed as a deliverable.
